claim: More than 85% of nucleosomes in mouse ES cells show intranucleosomally accessible DNA
quote: more than 85% of nucleosomes exhibit intranucleosomally accessible DNA

claim: Digestion-based mapping cannot distinguish a true hexasome from a distorted or unwrapped nucleosome
quote: Digestion is especially problematic when mapping subnucleosomes: a hexasome-sized fragment could be derived from a true hexasome; from a nucleosome with increased DNA accessibility between a single H2A–H2B dimer and the H3–H4 tetramer; or from transient unwrapping of DNA at nucleosomal entry and exit sites

claim: Short-read single-molecule MTase footprinting is capped by Illumina read length and dinucleotide-specific MTases
quote: are limited by the maximum read-length (600 bp) for Illumina sequencers, and by the use of MTases specific to GpC or CpG dinucleotides

claim: SAMOSA footprints chromatin with the nonspecific adenine MTase EcoGII read out by PacBio sequencing
quote: uses the nonspecific adenine MTase EcoGII and PacBio sequencing to footprint chromatin fibres

claim: Raising the transition probability t yields successively smaller footprint calls (subfootprints)
quote: Plotting the distributions of called footprint sizes across a wide range of t values confirmed that increasing t results in successively smaller footprint calls

claim: IDLI is named for iteratively scoring footprinted molecules
quote: We refer to this computational strategy, which depends on iteratively scoring footprinted molecules, as Iteratively Defined Lengths of Inaccessibility, or IDLI.

claim: Classification was applied to 795,765 nucleosomes from 145,065 E14 mouse ES cell fibres
quote: We applied this approach to 795,765 sampled nucleosomes from 145,065 sampled E14 mouse ES cell chromatin fibres.

claim: Clustering gave 14 nucleosome types grouped into seven self-similar groups I-VII
quote: resulted in 14 clusters, which we hereafter refer to as ‘nucleosome types’

claim: 86.6% of footprints fall into groups II-VII, showing some intranucleosomal accessibility
quote: the majority (86.6% of footprints falling into groups II–VII) of nucleosomes in E14 mouse ES cells show some degree of intranucleosomal DNA accessibility

claim: Cluster III-2 nucleosomes are accessible at SHL plus/minus 2
quote: which are nucleosome core particles accessible at SHL ±2

claim: Cluster II-2 nucleosomes are accessible at SHL plus/minus 3.5
quote: for cluster II-2 footprints, which are nucleosome core particles accessible at SHL ±3.5

claim: Highly accessible types are enriched in MNase-ChIP hexasome/hemisome fractions; least accessible in mononucleosome fractions
quote: suggesting that these group V–VII nucleosomes are bona fide subnucleosomal species

claim: The H1 TKO model ablates three of six linker histone genes, cutting chromatin-bound linker histone by about 50%
quote: a mouse ES cell model in which three of six linker histone genes were genetically ablated (H1 triple knockout; TKO), resulting in a reduction of around 50% in linker histone on chromatin

claim: Group I nucleosomes are chromatosomes containing linker histone H1
quote: we conclude that group I nucleosomes reflect chromatosomes that contain linker histone H1

claim: In vitro, group I nucleosomes are enriched with H1 and more so with H1 plus HMGB1
quote: These results suggest that group I nucleosomes seen in vivo represent nucleosomes that are bound by both H1 and HMGB1, or another HMG-box protein.

claim: Group I types are enriched for homeodomain binding motifs
quote: Group I nucleosome types were enriched for homeodomain binding motifs

claim: Groups II and III are uniquely enriched for forkhead family motifs
quote: and III nucleosome types were uniquely enriched for forkhead family motifs

claim: Groups IV and V are enriched for E-box binding motifs
quote: Group IV and V nucleosome types were enriched for E-box binding motifs

claim: The shortest footprints, groups VI and VII, are enriched for C2H2 zinc finger motifs
quote: were enriched for motifs recognized by C2H2 zinc finger (ZF) class TFs

claim: Bound CTCF motifs are enriched for subnucleosome and short footprints; CTCF degradation loses them
quote: Depletion of CTCF protein (Fig. 4g, bottom row) resulted in a significant loss of short footprints

claim: CTCF directly regulates nucleosome composition toward partially unwrapped states
quote: These analyses suggest that CTCF directly regulates the composition of structurally distinct nucleosomes to favour partially unwrapped states.

claim: NIPBL depletion alters nucleosome types globally but not specifically at CTCF sites
quote: Although depletion of NIPBL did alter nucleosome-type distributions significantly (suggesting that global loop extrusion has a role in regulating nucleosome structure), the observed effects were not specific to CTCF sites

claim: SOX2 depletion paradoxically decreases inaccessible nucleosome species, implying SOX2 stabilizes nucleosomes
quote: These results suggest that SOX2 protein stabilizes nucleosomal species in its vicinity.

claim: H3K4me3 promoters are enriched for types VI and VII; minor satellites for clusters I-2 and II-4
quote: In mouse minor satellite sequences, we observed a significant enrichment for clusters I-2 and II-4

claim: Nucleosome type enrichment scales with gene expression quintile at TSSs
quote: Enrichment or depletion of nucleosome types scaled with gene expression level

claim: Endoderm differentiation increases focally accessible and breathable subnucleosomes at FOXA2 sites
quote: These included increased representation of nucleosomes with focal accessibility within the nucleosome core particle (II-1 OR = 1.106, q = 1.58 × 10−05), and breathable subnucleosomes

claim: In vivo work used hepatocytes from 7 mice including a Foxa2 allele lacking its nucleosome-interacting domain
quote: heterozygous for a Foxa2 allele lacking a crucial nucleosome-interacting domain

claim: A histone-binding domain of FOXA2 directly contributes to distortion at its binding sites in vivo
quote: We conclude that nucleosome distortion occurs at cell-type-specific regulatory elements in vivo, and that a histone-binding domain of FOXA2 directly contributes to nucleosome distortion at associated binding sites.

claim: Homotypic trinucleosome arrangements are enriched in active chromatin, e.g. VI-VI-VI in H3K4me1
quote: including an enrichment of ‘homotypic’ arrangements specifically in active versus repressed epigenomic domains

claim: Short DNA protections most likely come from H2A-H2B dimers, with a quantifiable TF contribution
quote: Our pipeline also classifies short DNA protections; given the raw abundance of these protections, these are most likely to be a result of the histone H2A–H2B dimer

claim: TF-specific co-accessibility analysis needs greater SAMOSA coverage at target TF sites
quote: we stress that a comprehensive, TF-specific co-accessibility analysis will require SAMOSA data with increased genomic coverage specifically at target TF-binding sites

claim: IDLI detects altered pioneer TF-nucleosome interaction even with one functional FOXA2 copy present
quote: these findings also suggest that IDLI is sensitive enough to detect altered pioneer TF interactions with the nucleosome, even in the presence of a functional copy of the protein in the nucleus
